scenes.title: A press gives a physical click
Grid, motion, and timing decide gesture

vo.text: A tap clicks. A swipe scrolls. The touchpad has no buttons, yet it knows the difference.
Under the surface, a grid of capacitive electrodes watches your finger.
Each finger changes the electrical signal at its position on the grid.
A controller scans the whole grid many times per second to track where you touch.
Software then compares position over time. A short stationary touch is a tap.
A continued movement in one direction becomes a swipe, with speed setting scroll amount.
Pressing harder flexes the pad against a physical switch for a firm click.
So a scanned grid, tracked motion, and timing turn finger movement into tap or swipe.
